learning_outcomes.text: The student/graduate describes the fundamental concepts from general linguistics and correlates them with elements from a particular language.
The student/graduate describes and classifies the main concepts and linguistic theories referring to the phonetic, lexical, syntactic, semantic, and pragmatic system of the English language.
The student/graduate distinguishes linguistic standards and norms and specific terminology for different professional contexts in the English language.

The student/graduate identifies the linguistic and terminological particularities of different types of text (commercial and industrial documentation, personal documents, journalism, fiction, government documents, etc.).
The student/graduate describes the elements relevant to the culture and civilization of the peoples whose language they study.
The student/graduate applies methodological and theoretical models specific to the study of natural languages.
The student/graduate applies the main linguistic concepts and theories in producing texts in the English language.
The student/graduate applies the standards and norms of the English language.

The student/graduate corrects texts in the teaching language of the study program, translates different types of texts from one language to another, preserving the meaning and nuances of the original text, without additions/modifications/omissions.
The student/graduate contextualizes the English language in its cultural environment, adequately interprets cultural references, and adopts a broader perspective on cultural diversity.
The student/graduate translates orally or in writing from English to Romanian and back in broad, semi-specialized fields of interest.
The student/graduate drafts and edits scientific texts, academic scientific papers on different topics, avoiding wrong behaviors such as falsification and plagiarism.
The student/graduate uses appropriate expressions and words in producing texts in the English language.
The student/graduate autonomously uses specific terminology from different professional contexts in English and identifies the appropriate terminology to be used.
The student/graduate coherently and argumentatively expresses opinions and analyses about culture and civilization in discussions, essays, or presentations, adequately using specialized terminology.
The student/graduate efficiently uses glossaries and dictionaries on paper or electronic format, as well as databases.

The student/graduate respects ethical principles, norms, and values in the correct and timely execution of professional tasks, by adopting a rigorous, efficient, and responsible work strategy in making decisions to solve problems.
The student/graduate integrates into the work group and applies effective relationship and work techniques in multidisciplinary teams.
The student/graduate continuously informs and documents themselves in their field of activity by adequately using effective lifelong learning methods and techniques.
The student/graduate develops professional projects in the field of engineering.

syllabus_topics: Grammar in use: Nouns, Adjectives, Adverbs, Prepositions, Verb tenses
Vocabulary in use: Daily life, People, Environment, Social interaction
teaching_methods: Discovery-based learning models facilitated by direct/indirect exploration of reality (experiment, demonstration, modeling)

assessment_methods.method: Preparation of a project / oral presentation

assessment_rules: Conditions for promotion include participation in seminars, assimilation of taught notions, and taking the final test. The final evaluation result for a discipline is determined by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Integer grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded, with a grade of 5 certifying the acquisition of minimal learning outcomes for a discipline and the granting of corresponding study credits.
bibliography: Murphy, R. (2019). English Grammar in Use (5th ed.). Cambridge University Press.
Ibbotson, M. (2008). Cambridge English for Engineering [Student's Book with Audio CDs]. Cambridge University Press.
Gangalakshmi, C. Rathika, B. & Saranraj, L. (2023). Professional English for Engineers (2nd ed.). Cengage India.
